study_name: Third-Party Developer Extension Integration Usability Study
methodology: Consented task-based evaluation with 3 external engineers across Python, Go, and TypeScript backgrounds. Participants implemented an integration plugin using only published contract documentation and the reference manifest specification.
task_description: Implement a custom external issue-tracker notification plugin: create valid plugin.yaml, write entrypoint with tool definition, install into AmberClaw plugin directory, verify capability restrictions, confirm high-risk approval interception, and test graceful revocation.

participants.feedback: Manifest schema was clear. Appreciated that capability strings like filesystem_read are validated strictly on startup rather than failing quietly at runtime.
Clear separation between non-sensitive environment variables and filtered host secrets. The JSON-RPC stdin/stdout interface avoided needing complex SDK dependencies.
High-risk tool interception via ToolApprovalManager functioned out of the box. Verified that unapproved actions remain in pending ticket status without timeout execution.
